best_for: Photographers who shoot raw and want a free developer with fine control over demosaicing, color and sharpening, and who are willing to spend time learning it.

points.title: Free under GPLv3
points.text: RawTherapee costs nothing and is open source under GPLv3, in over 15 languages.

points.title: Built for raw files
points.text: It edits in 32-bit floating point, can mix two demosaicing methods in one image, merges pixel-shift shots with ghost masking, and does dark frame, flat field and hot pixel fixes.

points.title: What 5.13 changed
points.text: The default working profile is now Rec2020 instead of ProPhoto, so some tools may react differently. LibRaw is now the default raw reader, with the older dcraw as a fallback, and Windows gains an Arm64 build.

points.title: Expect a learning curve
points.text: The project itself says it rewards people who take time to learn it. RawPedia, the online manual, and the forum are where answers live.

points.title: Mac floor is high on Apple silicon
points.text: On Apple silicon the Mac build needs macOS 26 Tahoe or newer; Intel Macs need macOS 12 Monterey. The app only starts from the Applications folder.

points.title: Few versions kept
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 4 versions, in x64 and Arm64 installers for all users. macOS and Linux list only 5.13. The Linux Flatpak names the RawTherapee Team, but Flathub does not mark it verified; the project also offers an AppImage.
